Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

REFERENCE NOTES
The Riverside Link volunteer transport group serves the villages of Alder Quay, Bellmere and Northwick, taking residents to medical appointments, food collection points and occasional community events. The September 2026 rota covers journeys from Tuesday 1 September through Wednesday 30 September. The coordinator, Nessa Vale, normally pairs one driver with each passenger booking. Drivers meet passengers at the agreed pickup point; they are not asked to enter homes or provide personal care. A return journey is a separate booking only when the notes below give a return time. The group has two cars and one wheelchair-accessible minibus, but the minibus is shared with the day centre and is not automatically available on every date.

Nessa is trying to finish the rota before the August 24 volunteer meeting. She has asked that proposed assignments be listed by date and pickup time, with the passenger destination and volunteer name beside each booking. If a booking lacks a suitable confirmed driver or vehicle, it should appear as still needing cover rather than being silently dropped. She wants a short note at the end identifying any details that need checking, especially where the record is incomplete. The September list is a working draft, not a confirmation to passengers; Nessa will call passengers and volunteers after reviewing it.

The current bookings include a Tuesday 1 September pickup at 08:10 from Alder Quay for Mr. Ivo Marsh’s 09:00 eye appointment at Bellmere Clinic. He needs a return pickup from the clinic at 10:20. On Thursday 3 September, Lila Penn has requested a 09:30 pickup in Northwick for a 10:15 blood test at the same clinic, with no return time recorded yet. Her daughter said she may be able to collect her, but that is not confirmed. On Friday 4 September, two residents, Edie Rowe and Salim Hoss, need separate pickups from Bellmere at 11:40 for the 12:30 community lunch in Alder Quay. No return time is listed for either passenger.

On Tuesday 8 September, there are two clinic bookings: Niko Bell needs a 07:45 pickup in Alder Quay for an 08:30 appointment, returning from Bellmere Clinic at 09:35; and June Arlen needs a 13:00 pickup in Northwick for an appointment at 13:45. June’s form says “please leave enough time for the hill road,” but does not give a return time. On Wednesday 9 September, Marnie Cole has asked for a 10:00 pickup at the Northwick library for the 10:30 food collection in Bellmere. Her note says, “I can carry one small bag, not the full crate.” A return trip at 11:15 is requested.

The bookings later in the month are as follows. Friday 11 September: pickup at 08:20 in Alder Quay for Tomas Wren’s 09:10 dental appointment in Northwick; return pickup at 10:05. Monday 14 September: Ruth Dyer needs a 14:10 pickup in Bellmere for a 15:00 appointment at Alder Quay Health Centre; no return time has been supplied. Thursday 17 September: pickup at 09:00 in Northwick for the 09:45 hearing-aid clinic in Bellmere for Bea Knox, with a requested return at 11:00. Tuesday 22 September: two separate pickups in Alder Quay, one for Owen Pike at 08:00 for an 08:45 clinic appointment, and one for Farah Saye at 13:20 for an appointment at 14:00. Owen’s form requests a return at 10:00; Farah’s form has no return information.

The final dated requests are Wednesday 23 September, when Marnie Cole needs a 10:00 pickup at the Northwick library for the 10:30 food collection, returning at 11:15, and Monday 28 September, when Edie Rowe needs a 12:15 pickup in Bellmere for the 13:00 community lunch in Alder Quay. Edie has requested a return pickup at 15:30. The lunch is at the same hall used on 4 September. The office received a message from the hall that the side entrance will be closed for repairs on 28 September; the accessible entrance is at the rear, but the ramp is temporarily steeper than usual. The hall has not yet confirmed whether that route will remain suitable for every mobility aid.

Volunteer availability is recorded below. Nessa Vale can drive a standard car on weekdays after 09:30, except 14 September, and cannot take the minibus. Arun Das is available on 1, 8, 11 and 22 September, but only until 12:00 on each date; he is approved to use either standard car and has completed the minibus induction. Mae Finch can drive on 3, 4, 9, 17 and 23 September, and is comfortable with the Northwick hill road. She can use a standard car, but her minibus assessment is still pending. “I can do the early clinic runs, but I need to be back in Bellmere by noon,” she wrote. The note does not state whether she means all clinic runs or only the dates she listed.

Jonah Reed is free on 1, 3, 8, 14, 17, 22 and 28 September and may drive either a standard car or the minibus. On 28 September, however, he can start only after 13:00. Hadi Noor is available on 4, 9, 11, 14, 23 and 28 September and can drive a standard car; he is not trained on the minibus. On 17 September he is available only until 10:30. Celia Moss can drive a standard car on 8, 9, 17, 22 and 23 September. She has not yet confirmed whether she can help on 22 September, so that date should not be treated as confirmed. Her message reads, “I should know after my appointment next week.” No other September availability has been supplied for volunteers.

Vehicle notes are limited. The two standard cars are available throughout September except that Car B is booked by the day centre on 9 September until 12:00 and on 28 September all day. The accessible minibus is held for the day centre on 3, 8, 14, 17 and 28 September. On 9 September the day centre may release it after 12:00, but the office has not confirmed this. The minibus has a side ramp and can take one wheelchair user plus a driver; there is no information about additional passengers or equipment. Mr. Marsh uses a folding cane, while Owen Pike’s booking form says he uses a wheelchair and must travel in the accessible minibus. No other passenger’s vehicle-access needs are stated. Do not infer that a standard car is suitable for someone whose needs have not been recorded.

1. Follow-up items already noted by Nessa:
   - Ask Lila Penn whether her daughter will provide the return trip on 3 September, and confirm the return time if volunteer transport is still needed.
   - Confirm return times for Edie Rowe and Salim Hoss on 4 September, Ruth Dyer on 14 September, and Farah Saye on 22 September.
   - Ask the day centre whether the minibus can be released after 12:00 on 9 September.
   - Check Celia Moss’s availability for 22 September before assigning her.
   - Confirm whether the rear entrance and steeper ramp at the hall are suitable for Edie Rowe on 28 September.

The office has not received updates to these notes since August 18. Nessa prefers that a draft distinguish confirmed information from questions still awaiting an answer, and she does not want a volunteer assigned to a time outside their stated availability. If two bookings overlap, show the conflict or leave one without cover rather than assuming that a driver can complete both. The notes do not give journey durations, so they should not be used to infer that a driver can make a second pickup immediately after another trip. The rota should make the known bookings easy to review without turning pending details into firm arrangements.", "output": "Create a draft volunteer transport rota for Riverside Link covering 1–30 September 2026, using the reference notes below.
